Pressure vessel inspection services: what Atlantis delivers

Atlantis provides the nondestructive examination that an API 510 pressure vessel inspection depends on. ASNT-certified technicians, under ASNT NDT Level III oversight, perform UT thickness at CMLs, corrosion mapping, PAUT, TOFD, MT including wet fluorescent MT, PT, VT and eddy current. Radiography is performed by licensed radiography crews. Results go to your API 510 Authorized Inspector, who stays inspector of record. We return a quote within 24 hours.

What is included in a pressure vessel NDE scope

Most vessel work falls into six scope types. One turnaround often combines several of them across a unit. The table shows what triggers each scope, the methods normally used and what you receive. Final method selection is agreed with your inspector against each vessel's credible damage mechanisms.

ScopeTypical triggerMethodsWhat you receive
On-stream thickness surveyThickness measurement inspection due; on-stream inspection in lieu of internalUT at CMLs, encoded corrosion mapping, profile RT on small nozzlesCML table with current and previous readings, C-scans, verified minimum per CML
External inspection supportExternal inspection cycle, insulation damage, corrosion under insulation concernVT, UT at inspection openings, mapping at stripped areasCondition photos, thickness at openings, a findings list for the inspector
Turnaround internal supportVessel open for internal inspectionVT, MT and wet fluorescent MT, PT, UT, PAUT on welds, eddy current on non-ferrous tube bundlesIndication reports with locations, weld maps, photos
Crack-focused examinationWet H2S, amine, caustic or cyclic service; earlier crackingWet fluorescent MT on internal welds, angle-beam UT, PAUT, TOFDIndication length and, where the technique allows, depth; location sketches
Repair and alteration NDEWeld repair, nozzle addition, reratingMT or PT before and after repair; RT or UT as the repair plan requiresAcceptance reports against the code the repair plan names
New-construction NDEASME Section VIII fabrication in a shop or on siteRT through licensed crews, UT or PAUT where the code allows, MT, PTExamination reports for the fabricator's quality control and its ASME Authorized Inspector

Every report is built in our own NDT reporting software. Each reading is tied to the vessel, CML, procedure, technician certification and instrument calibration. Thickness data exports in a format your inspection data management system can import. Mapped areas can also be placed on a 3D model of the vessel. See Digital Twin reporting.

What the NDE report pack contains

Your inspector writes the inspection report. Our job is to give them evidence they can accept without chasing anyone. Each vessel's NDE pack includes:

  • A CML table with nominal, previous and current readings, using your CML IDs.
  • C-scan images and the raw scan files for every mapped area, with datum records.
  • Indication reports with location, length and, where the technique allows, depth, plus weld maps and photos.
  • The procedure and technique sheet reference for every examination.
  • Technician certifications and instrument calibration certificates.
  • A deviations log: areas not examined, with the reason, such as no access or insulation left in place.

The deviations log matters more than it looks. An inspector who knows what was not examined can make a sound decision. One who assumes full coverage cannot.

Where NDE effort usually goes, by vessel type

The same plant can hold vessels that need very different examinations. This is a starting point for discussion with your inspector, not a substitute for a damage mechanism review.

Vessel typeTypical concernsWhere NDE effort usually goes
Amine contactors and regeneratorsAmine stress corrosion cracking at welds; wet H2S damage in some sectionsWet fluorescent MT on internal welds, angle-beam UT or PAUT from outside
Sour water strippers and overhead accumulatorsWet H2S damage, including blistering and hydrogen-induced cracking; under-deposit corrosion0° mapping to find mid-wall damage, wet fluorescent MT, PAUT
Separators, knock-out drums and scrubbersBottom and water-boot corrosion, liquid-level attack, erosion at inletsCorrosion mapping of bottom heads and boots, UT at inlet impingement areas
Air receiversInternal corrosion where condensate collectsUT mapping of the bottom head and lower shell, VT of drains and supports
DeaeratorsCracking at shell weldsWet fluorescent MT on internal welds, angle-beam UT
Heat exchanger shells and bundlesShell-side corrosion, tube wall lossUT on shells and channels, eddy current on non-ferrous tubes

How an engagement runs, step by step

  1. Send the vessel list. Equipment IDs, manufacturer's data reports or nameplate data, drawings with CML locations, the last two inspection reports, service and operating temperature, insulation, access, target dates and your inspector of record's contact.
  2. Receive a quote within 24 hours. The quote is written per vessel. It lists methods, crew size, days on site and the assumptions behind them, such as who provides scaffolding, insulation removal and vessel cleaning. Pricing is quote on request.
  3. Agree the scope with your inspector. We confirm methods per damage mechanism, any added CMLs and the areas that need crack-focused techniques. Our Level III issues the technique sheets.
  4. Pre-mobilisation pack. You receive procedures, technician certifications, instrument calibration certificates and, for radiography, the crew's licensing documents before anyone arrives. Your site issues permits and runs orientation.
  5. Field execution. On-stream work runs while the unit operates. Internal work fits the turnaround window. You get a daily progress note against the vessel list.
  6. Same-shift escalation. Any reading at or near the required thickness, and any crack-like indication, goes to your inspector before the crew leaves the vessel.
  7. Level III review and report. Data is reviewed under Level III oversight, and one report is issued per vessel.
  8. Data handover. CML readings and C-scan files go to your inspector in the agreed format, using your CML IDs.
  9. Next campaign. The same datums and CML IDs are used again, so the next corrosion rate compares like with like.

Want the inspection plan or technique selection checked before the crew is booked? Talk to a Level III.

Turnaround timing: when to bring the NDE provider in

On the Gulf Coast most vessel work is planned around spring and autumn turnarounds. NDE goes wrong when it is booked as a last-minute crew rather than planned as part of the work list. A workable sequence looks like this:

  • At work-list freeze. Share the vessel list and damage mechanism review. This is when crack-focused techniques, added CMLs and radiography exclusion zones get into the plan.
  • Before the outage. Run the on-stream thickness surveys and corrosion mapping while the unit is still running. Findings then shape the internal scope instead of surprising it.
  • During the outage. Internal examinations follow cleaning and entry permits vessel by vessel. Hold points for your inspector are agreed in advance, so a crew is never waiting on a decision.
  • After start-up. Reports are finalised, data loads into your inspection database, and any deferred items move into the next on-stream plan.

Who this service is for

  • Refineries and petrochemical plants along the Texas and Louisiana Gulf Coast. These sites usually have their own API 510 inspectors but need NDE crews for turnarounds and on-stream programmes.
  • Chemical plants, gas processing and midstream sites. Separators, scrubbers, amine and dehydration vessels, and other services where cracking mechanisms sit alongside thinning.
  • LNG facilities and terminals. Process vessels, knock-out drums and receivers, often in coastal settings where external corrosion and CUI dominate.
  • Power plants. Deaerators, feedwater heaters and air receivers. Some of these fall under boiler or jurisdictional rules as well as the owner's programme.
  • Fabrication shops. New-construction NDE to ASME Section VIII. The acceptance criteria differ from in-service work; see ASME Section VIII Division 1 RT and UT acceptance.
  • Manufacturing, food and pharmaceutical sites. Air receivers, autoclaves and process vessels. Smaller sites often rely on an insurer's inspector and need NDE when that inspector asks for thickness or crack checks.

Scopes range from a few vessels on an insurer's list to a full unit turnaround.

How to compare pressure vessel inspection companies

Most bids look alike on the cover page. These questions separate them:

  • Is the scope written per vessel? A crew-day rate with no method list leaves method choice to whoever turns up.
  • Who accepts the data? The bid should name the inspector of record. If the same firm supplies both the inspector and the NDE crew, ask how that inspector stays independent of the crew's output.
  • Do methods match the damage mechanisms? Straight-beam thickness readings alone on a vessel in cracking service is a gap, however many readings are taken.
  • Are procedures and technique sheets Level III-approved? Ask for a sample technique sheet with the bid.
  • Are certifications current for each method? Check method, level, expiry and vision exam date for every named technician.
  • Is radiography properly licensed? RT crews must hold the radioactive material licence and radiographer certification the state requires.
  • Will the data fit your system? Your CML IDs, an export file and the raw C-scan files, not only a PDF.
  • How are urgent findings handled? The bid should promise same-shift escalation to your inspector.

Atlantis has completed 1,500+ inspection activities. A template for the report structure inspectors expect is in our free API 510 inspection report template.

Jurisdiction overlay: US states and Canada

API 510 is an owner-user code. Whether a state also inspects your vessels depends on where they sit. Federal OSHA's process safety management standard covers mechanical integrity for covered processes in every state. Beyond that, the rules vary.

  • Texas. Boilers are registered and inspected through the TDLR Boiler Program. Texas does not run a general state inspection programme for unfired pressure vessels, so vessel inspection is driven by PSM, insurers and owner programmes built on API 510. Confirm the status of a specific item with TDLR. See inspection services in Texas.
  • California. Cal/OSHA's Pressure Vessel Unit issues permits to operate for air tanks, LP-gas tanks and power boilers above set size and pressure thresholds. Permit inspections are performed by Cal/OSHA inspectors or qualified insurance company inspectors, under the Title 8 Unfired Pressure Vessel Safety Orders. See inspection services in California.
  • Louisiana, Illinois and Pennsylvania. Check the state's boiler and pressure vessel rules before scoping, because coverage of unfired vessels differs from state to state. See Louisiana, Illinois and Pennsylvania.
  • Owner-user inspection organisations. Where the jurisdiction accepts it, an owner-user accredited by the National Board under NB-371 can have its own commissioned inspectors carry out in-service inspections.

Canada notes. Pressure equipment is regulated by each province, generally through CSA B51, by bodies such as ABSA in Alberta, TSSA in Ontario and Technical Safety BC. Large owners may run integrity programmes that the provincial authority approves. NDT personnel on Canadian work are commonly certified to CAN/CGSB-48.9712. The CGSB closed on 1 April 2026, and NRCan's NDT Certification Body continues and issues CAN/CGSB-48.9712. Atlantis delivers Canadian work onsite; there is no Canadian office.

Common mistakes when buying vessel inspection

  • Buying technician hours instead of a scope. Without a method list per vessel, the cheapest bid is often the one that left out crack detection.
  • Letting the NDE contractor become the inspector by default. API 510 requires the inspector to evaluate and accept NDE results. A report with no named acceptor is not a completed inspection.
  • Renaming CMLs every campaign. New IDs break the corrosion rate history and force a fresh baseline.
  • Not sending the previous reports. The crew cannot spot a jump in corrosion rate on site if it cannot see the last readings.
  • Planning insulation removal and scaffolding late. NDE then becomes the critical path when the vessel opens.
  • Forgetting the small vessels. Air receivers and small process vessels outside the main unit often carry permit or insurer requirements of their own.
  • Treating fitness-for-service as part of the NDE bid. FFS is an engineering assessment. Scope it separately with a qualified assessor.

Frequently asked questions

Do you provide pressure vessel inspection services near me?

Atlantis is based in Houston and mobilises crews to client sites across the United States. We have no other US offices, so crews travel to your plant. Our state pages, from the inspection services hub, cover local regulators and cities.

What do pressure vessel inspection companies actually do?

Two different jobs often share the label. Inspection is the API 510 inspector's judgement on condition, intervals and repairs. Examination is the NDE that produces the evidence. Atlantis performs the examination and hands the results to your inspector.

Is Atlantis the API 510 Authorized Inspector on my job?

No. Your API 510 Authorized Inspector stays inspector of record and accepts the NDE results. Atlantis is the NDE provider working under ASNT Level III oversight.

Can you inspect a pressure vessel while it is running?

Yes. UT thickness and corrosion mapping are routinely done on-stream, within the temperature limits of the probe and couplant. Whether that on-stream work can replace an internal inspection is your inspector's decision under API 510. The API 510 standard summary sets out the conditions.

Do you perform NDE for new pressure vessel fabrication?

Yes. We perform RT through licensed radiography crews, UT or PAUT where the code allows, MT and PT for shops and site fabrication to ASME Section VIII. Reports go to the fabricator's quality control and its ASME Authorized Inspector.

Do you perform fitness-for-service or risk-based inspection?

No. API 579-1/ASME FFS-1 assessments and API 580/581 risk-based inspection are engineering services that Atlantis does not offer. We supply thickness grids and indication data in the form an assessor needs.

Can you inspect air receivers for a California permit?

Permit inspections in California are performed by Cal/OSHA Pressure Vessel Unit inspectors or qualified insurance company inspectors. If that inspector asks for thickness readings or other NDE, Atlantis can perform it and report to them.

What do you need from us to quote?

The vessel list, data reports or nameplate details, CML drawings, the last inspection reports, service conditions, access and insulation details, and your dates. We reply within 24 hours. Request an inspection quote.

How are results delivered?

As one report per vessel with CML tables, C-scans, indication reports, photos and certification records, plus a data export for your inspection database. See how intervals are then set in API 510 interval calculation explained. Ready to scope a campaign? Request an inspection quote.
